games.title: Metroid II: Return of Samus
games.note: Ends with the baby Metroid that sets up Super Metroid's story.

games.title: Metroid Fusion
games.note: Samus is stalked by the SA-X, a parasite copy of herself.

games.title: Metroid: Samus Returns
games.note: A remake of Metroid II by the Spanish studio that went on to make Metroid Dread.

games.title: Castlevania II: Simon's Quest
games.note: The first Castlevania with an open world, towns and a day-night cycle.

games.title: Castlevania: Rondo of Blood
games.note: A Japan-only PC Engine CD game until its official English release in 2007.

games.title: The Maze of Galious
games.note: Known as Knightmare II in Japan; two heroes explore a castle maze.

games.title: La-Mulana
games.note: A freeware tribute to 1980s MSX games, especially The Maze of Galious.

games.title: Faxanadu
games.note: Set on and inside a giant World Tree.

games.title: Xanadu
games.note: The second Dragon Slayer game; first released on Japan's PC-8801.

games.title: Cave Story
games.note: Made almost entirely by Daisuke 'Pixel' Amaya over about five years and released as freeware.

games.title: Shadow Complex
games.note: Set in the world of Orson Scott Card's novel Empire.

games.title: Axiom Verge
games.note: Made by one person, Thomas Happ.

games.title: Bionic Commando
games.note: The NES game, where you can't jump and must swing with a grappling arm.

games.title: Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night
games.note: Koji Igarashi's 2015 Kickstarter for it raised over $5.5 million.

games.title: Blasphemous
games.note: Its art draws on Seville's religious imagery and Goya's paintings.

games.title: Animal Well
games.note: Made by Billy Basso alone and published by Bigmode, the label of YouTuber Dunkey.

links.took: Samus, upgrade-gated exploration and the Metroid creatures.
links.added: A Game Boy hunt to wipe out every Metroid, tracked by an on-screen counter.

src.t: Wikipedia: Metroid II: Return of Samus

links.took: The baby Metroid that hatches at Metroid II's end, which drives Super Metroid's plot.
links.added: A return to Zebes with an auto-map, wall jumps and a much larger world.

links.took: Metroid II's story and planet SR388, rebuilt as a full remake.
links.added: A melee counter, free aiming and new Aeion abilities.

links.took: 2D Metroid exploration, controls and abilities, after an eight-year gap.
links.added: A guided mission structure and the SA-X, a copy of Samus that stalks her.

links.took: Its story, and stealth sequences that producer Yoshio Sakamoto wanted to expand on.
links.added: E.M.M.I. robots that hunt Samus through zones where she must run or hide.
links.extra: Sakamoto first tried to make Dread for the Nintendo DS around 2005.

links.took: MercurySteam; Nintendo revived Dread after seeing what the studio could do.
links.added: The first new 2D Metroid story in 19 years, with a slide and fast counters.

links.took: Acquiring tools that make the hero stronger, an idea Metroid pioneered following Zelda.
links.added: A side-scrolling alien maze where new gear opens sealed paths.
links.extra: Zelda came out months earlier; no developer statement says it shaped Metroid. Sakamoto named the film Alien as a big influence.

links.took: Side-scrolling run-and-jump action on the NES, which Super Mario Bros. popularized a year earlier.
links.added: Scrolling in every direction, upgrades that open new paths and a lone bounty hunter.
links.extra: No developer statement links them; this traces the genre, not a stated influence.

links.took: Huge levels and a morph-ball form, which Wikipedia attributes to Metroid.
links.added: Massive firepower, a lightning whip and freeform blasting on home computers.
links.extra: Wikipedia cites a German interview; it also names the arcade game Psycho-Nics Oscar for weapons and graphics.

links.took: A nonlinear world to explore, a design often compared to Metroid.
links.added: Towns, shops, a day-night cycle and cryptic clues from villagers.
links.extra: Asked about Metroid, designer Hitoshi Akamatsu cited The Maze of Galious instead.

links.took: An open, explorable action map; designer Hitoshi Akamatsu cited it when asked about influences.
links.added: Dracula's body parts to collect, hearts as money and experience levels.

links.took: Simon Belmont, the whip and Dracula's curse.
links.added: An open map with towns instead of linear stages.

links.took: Open exploration; Koji Igarashi said Simon's Quest's reception let Symphony be pitched to Konami.
links.added: One huge castle with RPG stats, equipment and an upside-down second castle.
links.extra: Wikipedia calls Symphony the first game to draw inspiration from Simon's Quest.

links.took: Belmont whip combat, subweapons and gothic stages.
links.added: CD audio, anime cutscenes, branching paths and a second playable heroine, Maria.

links.took: Its story and characters, Richter and Maria; Symphony is the direct sequel.
links.added: Alucard as hero, a single connected castle and RPG leveling.

src.t: Wikipedia: Castlevania: Symphony of the Night

links.took: Exploration and finding the item that unlocks the next area, per Koji Igarashi.
links.added: Applied that to a side-scrolling castle with RPG leveling and loot.
links.extra: Igarashi named A Link to the Past as the biggest influence.

links.took: Ability-gated 2D exploration, the reason players coined the word 'Metroidvania'.
links.added: RPG stats, gear drops and a gothic castle.
links.extra: Igarashi says he was thinking of Zelda, not Metroid, and finds the 'metroidvania' label strange.

links.took: Named by Team Cherry among the early games that shaped Hollow Knight from the start.
links.added: A hand-drawn insect kingdom with tough, precise combat.

src.t: William Pellen (Team Cherry), Red Bull Games

links.took: A huge connected map opened up by new movement abilities.
links.added: Maps you buy and fill in yourself, charms and a ruined insect kingdom.

src.t: William Pellen (Team Cherry), Red Bull Games

links.extra: Pellen: Super Metroid, Castlevania, Zelda II and Faxanadu were all big influences.

links.took: Exploration with towns of little characters and a vast world, per Ari Gibson and William Pellen.
links.added: A melancholy world told through scattered characters and lore.

src.t: Ari Gibson and William Pellen, Source Gaming
William Pellen (Team Cherry), Red Bull Games

links.took: A grim, side-view fantasy world, named by Team Cherry as a big early influence.
links.added: A buried insect kingdom, explored downward, with demanding combat.

src.t: William Pellen (Team Cherry), Red Bull Games
Ari Gibson and William Pellen, Source Gaming

links.took: Falcom's Xanadu: Hudson made Faxanadu as a spin-off side story.
links.added: Side-scrolling action on the NES, set around a giant World Tree.

links.took: Side-scrolling action-RPG exploration, a comparison Wikipedia notes.
links.added: One long climb up a World Tree, with towns, shops and dungeons.
links.extra: A comparison, not a stated influence; both came out in Japan in 1987.

links.took: The old-fashioned feel of games Daisuke Amaya played as a child, such as Metroid.
links.added: A heartfelt story, weapons that level up and a cast of rabbit-like Mimigas.

links.took: Named with Metroid among the childhood games Cave Story was meant to recall.
links.added: Hidden endings and a short, dense world made by one person.

links.took: Its gameplay; Donald Mustard called Super Metroid 'the pinnacle of 2D game design'.
links.added: Unreal Engine 3 graphics, with shooting into the background as well as sideways.
links.extra: The team spent its first month replaying Metroid games.

links.took: Many cues from the Metroid series; the team spent its first month replaying those games.
links.added: A modern thriller in a hidden underground base, rendered in 3D.

links.took: Ability-gated exploration and leveling, which Wikipedia says inspired its gameplay.
links.added: A modern thriller setting with guns, gadgets and a hidden enemy base.

links.took: Ability-gated alien exploration and a graphical style drawn from Metroid.
links.added: A gun that glitches enemies and terrain, and a sci-fi mystery about reality.
links.extra: Wikipedia cites a 2012 GameSpot preview. IGN's review felt it was too close to Metroid.

links.took: Run-and-gun weapon variety, listed among the games it borrows from.
links.added: Dozens of odd guns tied to exploration rather than score.

links.took: Swinging with a grapple, one of the NES games it borrows from.
links.added: Grappling combined with a remote drone and short teleport dashes.

links.took: Sprawling sci-fi underground maps, one of the NES games it draws on.
links.added: A lone scientist on foot, plus a small drone for tight passages.

links.took: Koji Igarashi, former Castlevania producer, and the post-Symphony Castlevania formula.
links.added: A crowdfunded castle, a heroine who absorbs demons' powers, and 3D graphics.

src.t: Wikipedia: Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night

links.took: Exploration-first design; Igarashi says Zelda inspired his work on Castlevania and Bloodstained.
links.added: Shard powers and crafting in a gothic castle.

links.took: A connected gothic world with ability-gated paths; Eurogamer's review called it a take on Castlevania.
links.added: Grim Spanish Catholic imagery and art inspired by Goya.
links.extra: The developers cite Seville's religious art rather than games.

links.took: Tough melee, a death penalty you must recover and cryptic lore; GameSpot's review called it 'Darker Souls'.
links.added: 2D pixel art and a world built on Andalusian religious art.

links.took: The Metroidvania structure Symphony popularized: one map gated by abilities and gear.
links.added: Randomly assembled levels and permadeath, a mix it calls a 'roguevania'.
links.extra: Its Return to Castlevania expansion includes a secret level inspired by Symphony of the Night.

links.took: Ability-gated exploration, from the childhood games Billy Basso drew on.
links.added: A dark, hand-drawn well full of animals, secrets and odd tools like bubbles.

links.took: Item-based discovery, from a childhood favorite Basso named.
links.added: Almost no combat: you avoid creatures and solve puzzles with toys.

links.took: Named by Basso among childhood games he saw as having similar ideas.
links.added: Layers of secrets that players worked together to uncover.

links.took: A sense of discovery and secrets hidden in plain sight.
links.added: Layered puzzles so deep that players collaborated online to solve the last ones.

src.t: Wikipedia: Animal Well (citing a Thinky Games interview)

links.took: Secrets hidden in plain sight and the joy of discovery.
links.added: Pixel art with rich lighting and a world full of creatures to avoid.

src.t: Wikipedia: Animal Well (citing a Thinky Games interview)

links.took: Hiding secrets in plain sight, a quality Basso admired.
links.added: Applied it to a 2D metroidvania with animal-based puzzles.

src.t: Wikipedia: Animal Well (citing a Thinky Games interview)

links.took: Its MSX look and ruins to explore; GR3 Project set out to make 'something like' it.
links.added: Huge, cryptic puzzle-filled ruins and an archaeologist hero.

links.took: Speed and precision in movement, which Thomas Mahler credited to Super Meat Boy.
links.added: Painterly forest art and a metroidvania map built around fluid movement.

links.took: Its structure: Mahler said Ori owes far more to Super Metroid than to Zelda.
links.added: Soul Link save points you place yourself, and a heavy-hearted story.

links.took: Exploration and secrets from Mahler's favorite game, which the team grew up on.
links.added: A side-scrolling spirit guardian saving a dying forest.

links.took: Classic platformer feel; programmer David Clark named the Rayman and Metroid series as inspirations.
links.added: Bash, a move that launches Ori off enemies and projectiles.

src.t: Wikipedia: Ori and the Blind Forest
